difficultyRationale: exports and opens look similar but differ in compile-time versus run-time access and in whether private members are reachable through reflection.
prompt: A module declares directives for one of its packages, `p`. Which statements about `exports` and `opens` are true? Select all that apply.
explanation: exports controls compile-time and run-time access to the public and protected types of a package. opens controls run-time reflective access, including to private members, and does not grant compile-time access. A qualified form (to m) limits either directive to specific modules. Being exported alone does not allow deep reflection on private members.

options.text: `exports p;` makes the public types of `p` accessible to code in other modules at both compile time and run time.
options.explanation: That is the purpose of exports: it defines the accessible API of the module.

options.text: `opens p;` allows code in other modules to use reflection at run time to access all types and members of `p`, including private ones.
options.explanation: An open package allows deep reflection, for example setAccessible(true) on a private field.

options.text: `opens p;` also makes the public types of `p` accessible to other modules at compile time.
options.explanation: opens affects run time only. Without exports, other modules cannot compile against the package.

options.text: `exports p to m;` makes the package accessible only to module `m`.
options.explanation: This is a qualified export, which restricts access to the named module or modules.

options.text: If `p` is exported but not opened, another module can call `setAccessible(true)` on a private field of a class in `p`.
options.explanation: Reflective access to non-public members requires the package to be open. The call fails with InaccessibleObjectException.
